title: What a finger cue can predict
source_attribution: Adapted from Kai Joshua Miller, A library of human electrocorticographic data and analyses, Stanford Digital Repository, v11. Early portions of the data were selected, transformed, fitted and compared. Respect the privacy and confidentiality of participants.

ethics_and_original_study.methods: Original study statement appears verbatim on page 4 of the paper.

score_convention: Within each experiment lower error is better. A positive signed gain means comparator error minus aligned-model error. The final column of paper Table 3 reports the opposite sign as extra repeat error.

later_value_in_one_person.units: Stored sensor counts at a single future tick at +120 nominal ms. Each normalized error divides by the training target standard deviation for its digit.
later_value_in_one_person.intervals: within-record paired, 5000 circular moving-block bootstrap samples of consecutive trial triplets

movement_size_in_one_person.units: Mean absolute difference between adjacent future sensors at +40, +80, +120 and +160 nominal ms, in counts per 40 ms step. Each normalized error divides by the training movement-size standard deviation for its digit.

movement_size_in_five_people.units: Same unsigned counts per 40 ms step. Scaled errors divide by each held person’s early per-digit root-mean-square size, floored at one count per step.
movement_size_in_five_people.intervals: Prespecified equal-person 95% descriptive percentile intervals enumerate all 5^5 resamples with replacement. Each fold reuses training people from other folds. These do not quantify external population precision.

independent_per_person_comparisons.unit: Positive values favor the correctly paired model. Within each recording, the descriptive 95% intervals resample blocks of three consecutive trials or disjoint quartets with wraparound, 5,000 draws. All models and people remain fixed. The resampling count n is the number of trials or quartets, not number of forecast cutoffs.
